Situation1: They send an occasional text to check in with their parents over the weekend.
Expectation2: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation2: You get a frantic call from your friend whose car has broken down on the side of the highway late at night, and they need you to come get them immediately.
Story: It was late Saturday night when my phone buzzed with a text from my stepdad: “Hope you’re having a good weekend. Let us know you’re okay.” I knew he and Mom worried if I didn’t check in, especially since I’d promised to keep in touch more often. I started typing a quick reply, but before I could hit send, my phone rang. It was Jamie, my best friend. Her voice shook as she told me her car had broken down on the highway, miles from home, and she was scared. She needed me to come get her right away. I glanced at the clock—almost midnight. If I left now, I’d be gone for hours, and I’d probably forget to text my parents. But if I stayed to message them, Jamie would be alone and afraid even longer. My chest tightened as I stared at my phone, torn between the promise I’d made to my family and the loyalty I owed my friend.
